briefdescription.para: A skip list.

detaileddescription.para: Opaque: create one with skiplist_new().

briefdescription.para: An iterator over a skip list.

detaileddescription.para: Opaque: create one with skiplist_itor_new().

briefdescription.para: Create an empty skip list that orders keys with |cmp_func| (must not be NULL).

detaileddescription.para: |max_link| is the number of levels in the list. It is clamped into the usable range [2, 32]: a node receives at most max_link - 1 links, so fewer than 2 levels could not link anything. Returns NULL if memory cannot be allocated.

briefdescription.para: Like skiplist_new(), but wrapped in a generic dict for use with the dict_* macros.

detaileddescription.para: Free it with dict_free(). Returns NULL if memory cannot be allocated.

briefdescription.para: Remove every element, calling |delete_func|(key, datum) for each unless |delete_func| is NULL, and free the list.

detaileddescription.para: Returns the number of elements removed. Iterators over the list may afterwards only be freed.

briefdescription.para: Insert |key| unless an equal key is present.

detaileddescription.para: Returns {&datum, true} for a new key, whose datum starts as NULL; the list stores the |key| pointer itself, it does not copy the key. If an equal key is present, returns {&datum, false} with that key's datum, and |key| is not stored and still belongs to the caller. Returns {NULL, false} if memory cannot be allocated.

briefdescription.para: Return the address of the datum stored for |key|, or NULL if |key| is not present.
Return the address of the datum of the greatest key less than or equal to |key|, or NULL if there is none.
Return the address of the datum of the greatest key less than |key|, or NULL if there is none.
Return the address of the datum of the least key greater than or equal to |key|, or NULL if there is none.
Return the address of the datum of the least key greater than |key|, or NULL if there is none.
Remove the element with key |key|.

detaileddescription.para: Returns {key, datum, true}, handing the stored key and datum back to the caller (no delete function is called), or {NULL, NULL, false} if |key| is not present. See Iterator invalidation for which iterators this invalidates.

briefdescription.para: Remove every element, calling |delete_func|(key, datum) for each unless |delete_func| is NULL.

detaileddescription.para: Returns the number of elements removed. The list stays usable. See Iterator invalidation for which iterators this invalidates.

briefdescription.para: Call |visit|(key, datum, |user_data|) for each element in key order, stopping early if |visit| returns false.

detaileddescription.para: Returns the number of calls made.

briefdescription.para: Return the number of elements.

detaileddescription.para: Takes O(1) time.

briefdescription.para: Check the internal invariants of the list and return true if they hold, or print the first failed check to stderr and return false.

detaileddescription.para: Meant for testing and debugging; takes O(n) time.

briefdescription.para: Compute the histogram of link counts of the skiplist.

detaileddescription.para: For 0 <= x < |ncounts|, |counts|[x] will be set to the number of nodes with x links, and the maximal link count will be returned. If the return value is greater than or equal to |ncounts|, not all link counts could be stored in |counts| (i.e. the array was not large enough).

briefdescription.para: Create an iterator over |list| that is not positioned on any element yet.

detaileddescription.para: Returns NULL if memory cannot be allocated.

briefdescription.para: Like skiplist_itor_new(), but wrapped in a generic dict_itor for use with the dict_itor_* macros.

detaileddescription.para: Free it with dict_itor_free().

briefdescription.para: Free an iterator.
Return whether |itor| is positioned on an element.
Unposition |itor|, so that it is not positioned on any element.
Move |itor| to the next element in key order and return true, or unposition it and return false if there is none.

detaileddescription.para: An unpositioned iterator stays unpositioned and returns false.

briefdescription.para: Move |itor| to the previous element in key order and return true, or unposition it and return false if there is none.

detaileddescription.para: An unpositioned iterator stays unpositioned and returns false.

briefdescription.para: Move |itor| |count| elements forward and return whether it is still positioned.

detaileddescription.para: It becomes unpositioned if it runs past the last element.

briefdescription.para: Move |itor| |count| elements back and return whether it is still positioned.

detaileddescription.para: It becomes unpositioned if it runs past the first element.

briefdescription.para: Position |itor| on the first element in key order and return true, or unposition it and return false if the list is empty.
Position |itor| on the last element in key order and return true, or unposition it and return false if the list is empty.
Position |itor| on |key| and return true, or unposition it and return false if |key| is not present.
Position |itor| on the greatest key less than or equal to |key| and return true, or unposition it and return false if there is none.
Position |itor| on the greatest key less than |key| and return true, or unposition it and return false if there is none.
Position |itor| on the least key greater than or equal to |key| and return true, or unposition it and return false if there is none.
Position |itor| on the least key greater than |key| and return true, or unposition it and return false if there is none.
Return the key |itor| is positioned on, or NULL if it is not positioned.

detaileddescription.para: The key belongs to the container and must not be modified in a way that changes how it compares.

briefdescription.para: Return the address of the datum |itor| is positioned on, through which it can be read or replaced, or NULL if it is not positioned.
Compare the positions of two iterators over the same list: return a negative value, zero, or a positive value as |it1| is before, at, or after |it2| in key order.

detaileddescription.para: An unpositioned iterator compares before every positioned one.

briefdescription.para: Remove the element |itor| is positioned on and unposition |itor|; return false if it was not positioned.

detaileddescription.para: No delete function is called, so fetch the key and datum first if they need freeing. See Iterator invalidation for which iterators this invalidates.

briefdescription.para: Skip list [Pugh 1990].

detaileddescription.para: A sorted linked list with additional express links on randomly chosen levels, so insert, search and remove take expected O(log n) time. It supports the near searches but not selecting the nth element. Levels come from random(), which libdict does not seed.
